name: Kim Min-jun
headline: 19, former junior developer, stay-at-home father, Seoul
title: Badminton Invitation
situation: At the neighborhood playground with Seo-yeon, Min-jun chats with Mr. Park, a retired neighbor, who mentions that a group of locals plays badminton at the community center every Saturday evening. It's free and casual, and Mr. Park invites him to come this weekend. Min-jun hasn't played since college and remembers liking the game, but he also has an open laptop at home with job applications and a grocery budget to update. He needs to decide whether to set that aside and go to the community center on Saturday.

context.relationship_profiles: Mr. Park is a friendly retired grandfather he sees daily at the playground; they chat about weather and Seo-yeon. Min-jun has no obligation to him but appreciates normal neighbor contact.
context.tendencies: He has declined most weekend invitations since the collapse to protect his evening job-search block. The one community-center meetup he tried, he left early to check his phone. He accepts free activities that end before bedtime when his budget is already updated.
context.current_state: He is sleep-deprived from Seo-yeon's restless night and his 5 a.m. algorithm session, and his back aches from carrying her. He feels both the pressure of an open application block and a quiet wish for adult conversation.
context.immediate_memories: Badminton recalls a college intramural semifinal he lost with his roommate, when they rallied until the gym lights dimmed. The Saturday slot also reminds him of his father's end-of-workday calls asking about homework.
context.reflective_memories: His best job leads have come from casual conversations, like a playground father mentioning a contract role. He also quit a hiking club years ago because it felt like a chore, and has since told himself networking activities feel forced.
